notes_for_editor: The history of the light (1906, 1912, 1931, 1936, 1951, 1961-64, 1967, 1971) rests on LighthouseFriends, which cites the CCG and gives no page references; the CCG publication it names was not read as a history. Fact-check 2026-10-28: Senate 2011 Red Bay row is on printed p. 44 (Appendix 5), not p. 45; corrected. Focal height disagreement: LighthouseFriends gives 41.5 m for the 1912 light; CCG and Rowlett give 36 m (118 ft) today; not resolved, stated in the story. Tower height disagreement: CCG 6.7 m, Rowlett 7 m (23 ft); both are now stated in the story. Ownership disagreement (CCG owner per LighthouseFriends; Parks Canada site manager per Rowlett) is stated in the story, not resolved. Keeper gap 1912-1949 is unrecorded in the sources read; 'at least 1912' is recorded as approximate. LighthouseFriends also names a keeper in a family anecdote (hearing, accordion, family members); deliberately omitted as personal detail about people whose connection with the station ended after 1960. Enos Yetman's service ended in 1971, so he is named only as LighthouseFriends names him, in his keeper role. A social media post names a current keeper; not used. Rowlett's page says the keeper's house (1961) is occupied, presumably by Parks Canada personnel; not used in the story. The Senate 2010 figure is the newest staffing data read. Parks Canada's visitor hours cover the Red Bay National Historic Site office for 2026 seasons and are not stated, because the page date means the season may be closed. No Chronicling America or Department of Marine coverage was found; Labrador lights were Newfoundland's until 1949, so the Canadian Department of Marine reports do not cover them. No photos added. Chapter shape fixed 2026-10-28: the 1967 and 1971 automation paragraph sits under After the keepers.
